items.title: Colapinto carries a five-place grid penalty into the Bahrain GP at Sepang
items.summary: FIA Document 66 converted Franco Colapinto's 10-second Azerbaijan Race penalty into a five-place drop at the next race in which he participates. Formula1.com identifies that as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia; the checked-out 2026 calendar places the event at Sepang on 4 October.
items.why_it_matters: This is a confirmed carry-over sanction, not a Bahrain stewards' decision or a predicted grid position. Wait for qualifying and the official starting grid before stating where Colapinto will start.

items.title: Formula 1 returns to Sepang for a different Bahrain Grand Prix
items.summary: Formula1.com's race-week briefing places the relocated Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang for 2–4 October, with George Russell arriving after his Azerbaijan victory and the venue presenting a new test for much of the current field.
items.why_it_matters: Sepang's return changes the circuit context: compare current weekend evidence with the venue's historic Malaysian races, but do not carry over Bahrain-specific performance assumptions.

sources.label: Formula1.com: five storylines ahead of the Bahrain GP in Malaysia

items.title: Pirelli nominates C2, C3 and C4 for Sepang's return
items.summary: For the Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang (2–4 October), Pirelli selected C2 Hard, C3 Medium and C4 Soft. It describes Kuala Lumpur's asphalt as particularly abrasive and not resurfaced since the last F1 race there in 2017, while rating its tyre stress as medium relative to the calendar.
items.why_it_matters: This is the compound nomination and Pirelli's track-level tyre assessment, not a driver-by-driver race-set allocation; new and used sets remain unknown until post-qualifying evidence is published.
